title: The tick's rules tenant comes from LKB_TENANT_ID, but the candidates/calendar it schedules come from whatever tenant LKB_API_KEY belongs to; nothing asserts the two are the same
evidence: The tick has no tenant field of its own: items come from GET /meeting-candidates and /calendar/upcoming under LKB_API_KEY (one tenant by key), while the join-rules file is opened for LKB_TENANT_ID. If the two differ, tenant X's rules would be applied to tenant Y's meetings (veto-only, so it can only remove, but it would remove or keep the wrong events). Not observable inside the unit: the API key's tenant is not readable client-side.
fix_direction: Before enabling LKB_JOIN_RULES_ENFORCE the operator must confirm LKB_TENANT_ID is the API key's tenant, or a later unit adds a whoami call / key-tenant check at tick start (with enforcement on, a mismatch should be unevaluable). Approver/operator decision.

title: An unrecognised non-empty LKB_JOIN_RULES_ENFORCE value (e.g. Fail-Closed, FAIL-CLOSED, ' fail-closed', true) silently leaves enforcement OFF: no log line at startup or per tick
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules-enforce.ts parseJoinRulesEnforce / enforceJoinRules (off returns selection with no log)
evidence:
Real tick, store holding optedOutEventIds:[g1], joinRulesEnforce in ["Fail-Closed","FAIL-CLOSED"," fail-closed","fail-closed ","fail-open
","true","1","yes"]: g1 stays scheduled and the tick log contains 0 lines mentioning the setting or rules (checker test: 'UNRECOGNISED log lines mentioning rules/enforce: 0'). An operator who typed a variant believes opt-outs are honoured while none are: the false assurance this unit exists to remove.
fix_direction: Before anyone sets a value: when the raw value is a non-empty string (after no trimming) that is not exactly off/fail-closed/fail-open, log one loud line per tick: 'LKB_JOIN_RULES_ENFORCE has unrecognised value: enforcement is OFF' (value truncated, control chars stripped), and keep behaviour OFF (strict matching is the safe direction; do NOT lenient-parse). Empty/absent stays silent. Add a test; default-path behaviour for empty/absent must stay byte-identical.

title: Note (low, not a unit): a non-synchronous evaluator result is read as keep even under fail-closed, silently; unreachable in production today (io.evaluate is a test seam, real evaluator is synchronous)
evidence: Real tick, evaluate returns Promise.resolve({action:'skip',...}): fail-closed and fail-open both schedule g1, 0 warnings.
fix_direction: If an async evaluator is ever introduced, under fail-closed a non-sync result must be rules-unevaluable. Recorded only; not a pulled unit.
